_: Seam 2. Every hard rule the controller runs under, in one list. Adding a rule is appending one entry; suspending one is flipping `active`. The `effect` field names the mechanism in model.ts that reads it, so there is never a search for where a rule bites.

constraints.name: transformer_limit
constraints.why: The distribution transformer's rating. Crossing it is what the whole system exists to prevent, and it is also the number the demand charge is written against.

constraints.name: never_curtail
constraints.why: Lifts, water, fire and medical devices are never shed. Any device carrying one of these tags has its `curtailable` flag forced false in the derived registry, whatever the device entry says, so the guarantee is structural rather than a promise. Note this governs SHEDDING, not moving: a pump run at 08:00 instead of 14:00 is deferred, not curtailed, which is why the pumps stay in the deferrable pool.

constraints.name: critical_load_floor
constraints.why: A minimum draw that must be met regardless of the ceiling. Off by default. Turn it on and set a value when a load must keep running rather than merely not be shed — 'the water pump must run twice daily' is this entry.

constraints.name: deferral_cap_per_flat
constraints.why: No flat may be asked to wait more than eight times in a month. A system that saves eighteen percent by always deferring the same six flats gets voted out at the next general body meeting.

constraints.name: deadline_honoured
constraints.why: Every deferred device finishes before its own deadline, read from the device registry. A geyser held at 18:30 with a 06:00 deadline is a scheduling decision; one held past 06:00 is a failure.

constraints.name: opt_out_respected
constraints.why: A flat that has opted out is never deferred, and the interface never hides it. Consent is a constraint, not a setting.
